hero.title: Uber × Navier — India's ride-hail leader, on the water
hero.subtitle: Six high-value India markets — all six on the map with sealed corridors and economics pending on new eastern/southeastern routes.
hero.what_we_do_together: An Uber-branded foiling water tier across Mumbai, Goa, Kerala backwaters, the Andaman islands, Kolkata's Hooghly waterfront and Chennai's ECR coast — booked in-app on sealed Atlas corridors.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, ~10x more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives next door; Kochi's electric Water Metro proves India's clean-ferry appetite; and India's busiest coastal flows - Mumbai<->Alibaug, Port Blair<->Havelock - run on slow, ageing diesel craft. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster.
multimodal_fit: Uber already runs the hard parts - real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing and a vast captain-partner network across India. A foiling water tier slots straight in: same app, captain-partners on the water, the water leg booked door-to-door with the Uber auto or bike to and from the jetty.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready; a factory in Turkey for supply; and a ~100-vessel network already proving the model in the Maldives - directly relevant to India's coastline and archipelagos. The water is the ownable surface Uber can lock down before its rivals reach it.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. markets.label: Andaman & Nicobar Islands
markets.summary: The Andamans are India's marquee island-hopping market - Port Blair to Havelock and Neil - and a natural Uber leisure surface. Inter-island transport runs entirely on diesel fast-ferries that sell out in season; an Uber foiling tier turns the busiest island-hop in India into a fast, silent, in-app trip.

hero.title: Uber x Navier - Andaman & Nicobar Islands on the water
hero.subtitle: Andaman & Nicobar Islands, foiling and in-app.
hero.what_we_do_together: Uber brings the in-app demand and the land first/last mile; Navier brings the silent foiling fleet. Together we put Andaman & Nicobar Islands's water in the Uber app.

partner_context.their_ambition: Uber is the established premium ride-hail leader extending its trusted brand into India's high-growth tourism geographies.
partner_context.their_pressure: Andaman inter-island transport is captive to diesel fast-ferries with no premium or clean tier.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling tier gives Uber an ownable island-hopping product on India's busiest tropical archipelago - Port Blair<->Havelock<->Neil - in-app.

markets.why_now: Andaman island tourism is booming on sold-out diesel ferries, the government is pushing connectivity, and Uber is extending its premium brand into high-growth tourism geographies.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: India's busiest island-hop - Port Blair<->Havelock - sells out every season on diesel fast-ferries, in coral-sensitive waters that reward clean propulsion, with no premium tier for Uber to own.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $149M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet - Pioneer II for harbour, coastal and island hops and Quanta-LR hybrids for the longer legs - plus captain training, the maintenance and certification path, and a uniform integration spec, all proven on the ~100-vessel Maldives network.
the_ask.partner_brings: India's largest premium ride-hail demand base, the trusted Uber brand and rider/guest relationship, and the six coastal and island markets - Mumbai, Goa, Kerala, the Andamans, Kolkata/Hooghly and Chennai/ECR - to launch the on-water tier.
the_ask.next_step: Pick a launch cluster - Mumbai is the recommended start - and scope a Phase-1 pilot on the entry corridor, then sequence the other markets as the network matures.

close.title: India's water tier - Uber's to own.
close.body: Uber leads India's roads; the coast, harbours, backwaters and island archipelagos are the next premium surface. A software-defined foiling fleet, already proven next door in the Maldives, lets Uber switch on the water cluster by cluster - and own it before rivals reach it.

end_state.headline: The water tier of Indian mobility - coast, harbours, backwaters and island archipelagos, owned by the leader.
end_state.addressable_footprint: India's high-value coastal and island clusters - Mumbai & the Konkan coast, Goa's rivers and beaches, Kerala's harbour and backwaters, the Andaman archipelago, the Kolkata/Hooghly waterfront and the Chennai/ECR coast.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II foiling vessels for harbour, coastal and island hops; Quanta-LR hybrids for the longer coastal line-hauls that need no charging infrastructure.
steady_state.corridors: Harbour and airport crossings, weekend-coast and island-hop runs, and inter-city coastal line-hauls (such as the Konkan run between Mumbai and Goa), all booked in the Uber app.
steady_state.note: At scale this reaches 60+ vessels across India's coastal clusters, in line with the network thesis; per-market fleet sizing and corridor economics are set out in each market's ladder.
